t: The expansive villa on the island of Po
d: For the superimposed loggias of the palace appear the footmen and the garzoni to the looms, to the works of the needle, to the works of the perfumes, to the games, to the concerts, grouped and posing as they will be later under the regiment of Borso in the fresh of Schifanoia. Each small company has its foggia, its office, its choral voice; and all for within the aerial architecture live almost swarms in an immense beehive. In the extense barco - which is spread with its nurseries, with its tanks, with its fishboards up to the edge of the island - Ugo d'Este, the son of the Marchese Nicolò III and of Stella de' Tolomei, he practiced at the shooting of the crossbow together with a matte of noble his peers. Often he errs the sign and s'adira. Green, one of the above, in the loggia, the choirs with a wandering lamentment. Each company responds to the voices with a response so much in response to the voices of the voices

The house of Nazareth appears, the simple house of Joachim and Anna, built of reddish stones with a door, with a window, with a fireplace, with an altar, that on the night of May the angels moved on their wings to the beach of Schiavonia and on the night of December to the opposite shore, to the brand of Ancona, within the forest of the laurels. By the wide-open door there is a shining between the presses and the lamps the black virgin, carved in the cedar wood by the hand of Luke the Evangelist covered with the precious garment woven of gold and gems. The walls of the hospices rise behind the sanctuary. From there the lauret shines the Adriatic sea. Against the limit of the pavilion, where monks and priests receive the offerings, is explained the rich pavilion of the pilgrim of Ferrara, distinguished by the Eagles and the fiordalisi estensi.

The bedroom is deep and rich. The large bed is wrapped in the curtains. The doubles are off. Sola burns a lantern placed on the floor, opposite the door. Parisina is lying in a carpet, near the lantern. Stick the elbows, narrow between the dagger closed her head, deceives the wait by reading the Romance of Tristan. The light illuminates the intense face and the open book on the body of the harp as on the lectern. The rest is in the shade. Above a scrawl The Green seems to sleep. The window is open to the beautiful night and to the hour of the verzieri in bloom. Believing to hear the furious step near the threshold that the low light marks of an indicator line, Parisina stoopes, stands on her knees, and listens throbbing. There is no edge of a known but remote choir on the night wind:

The secrets appear at the bottom of the tower. An archivolt over two tubby pillars, open in the majestic wall, lets the place of justice be seen through a firm and rugged iron gate. A vertical opening, long and narrow as a crossbow, is the only eye of the prison, but there passes no glimmer, being still night, a little before the morning. There is the prepared log, and the Justizer with his Manigolds and with his other People; and the presses v'ardono. Someone is not from here from the wall, from here from the ironed arch. Closed is the usciolo that from the manco side gives access to this part. Ugo and Parisina are from the other side from the gate, standing, both of them, connected so that they seem indissoluble. The voice of her, in the throat that is about to be cut, is fresh as the jubilus of the lark.
